title: Beyond Prompts: Runtime Contracts for Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.19549v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Coding agents act on repositories through shell commands and file edits, and teams steer them with written engineering rules. Industrial settings expect such rules to be enforced and their application to be evidenced, and a rule given as prompt text provides neither. We test whether executable contracts enforced while the agent works reduce rule violations compared with the same rules in the prompt, retrieved as guidance, or checked only after generation. Violations are scored by an oracle whose methods differ from the in-loop checks, and the oracle is validated by two human reviewers and a model reviewer. Across three studies on two model families (240, 112 and 108 runs), enforcement during execution produced no oracle-detected violation in 104 paired runs, against 21 to 55% of runs without rules, and no loss of functional correctness in the two confirmatory studies. translated_title: 超越提示词：编码智能体的运行时契约
translated_abstract: 编码智能体通过 shell 命令和文件编辑对代码仓库进行操作，团队则用书面工程规则来引导它们。工业场景期望这类规则能够被强制执行，并且其应用情况能够被证实，而以提示文本形式给出的规则两者皆无法提供。我们测试了在智能体工作时强制执行的可执行契约，与将相同规则置于提示词中、作为指导检索、或仅在生成后检查相比，是否能减少规则违规。违规行为由一个与循环内检查方法不同的预言机进行评分，该预言机由两名人工审查者和一个模型审查者验证。在针对两个模型系列的三项研究（240、112 和 108 次运行）中，执行期间的强制实施在 104 组配对运行中未产生任何预言机检测到的违规，而无规则时的违规率为 21% 至 55%，且在两项验证性研究中功能正确性没有损失。在针对已知失败场景任务的验证性研究中
tldr: 该论文提出在编码智能体工作期间强制执行的可执行契约，实验证明相比提示词规则、检索式指导或生成后检查，运行时强制执行能完全消除规则违规且不损失功能正确性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes executable contracts enforced at runtime while coding agents work, demonstrating through three studies that runtime enforcement completely eliminates rule violations compared to prompt-based rules, retrieved guidance, or post-generation checks, without any loss of functional correctness.
